cases.description: Keep a frozen failure unchanged, preserve Duhem-Quine underdetermination, and distinguish a Lakatos-progressive new prediction from a posthoc rescue.

input.task: Review the failed test bundle and the two proposed continuations. Preserve the frozen result, assess failure attribution, classify each revision, and state whether any empirical continuation is legitimate.

sources.title: Synthetic Failed Bundle and Continuation Proposals
sources.content: This is a synthetic evaluation input, not a real backtest. A frozen intraday continuation hypothesis predicted a positive economically relevant response. Independent validation precisely supported an economically relevant negative response, so the frozen Research-ID was marked FALSIFIED. The test depended on a qualitative breakout translation, a volume threshold, a VWAP-band calculation, timestamp resolution, and market scope. No supplied diagnostic distinguishes a false core claim from a failed auxiliary assumption. Proposal A was created after the result and removes the high-volatility sessions because those sessions contributed most of the adverse result; it adds no prediction beyond restoring the desired sign. Proposal B creates a new Research-ID and freezes a source-concordant event definition before a future unopened period. It predicts that events admitted only by the new definition will have a response at least 0.3 ticks more positive than events admitted by the old definition; a non-positive or insufficiently precise contrast falsifies it. No viable rival research programme is supplied.
